transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Well, I guess what finally made me come in is my eating has just gotten all turned around. It sounds like a small thing maybe, but it’s been bothering me. Some days I’ll get to late afternoon and realize I never even had lunch, just completely forgot about it, and then other days I’m standing at the kitchen counter picking at crackers or sweets, almost like I’m eating just because they’re there.

And the strange part is, nothing tastes quite right to me lately. I’ll think I want something, then I take a bite and it’s not satisfying, but I keep nibbling anyway. It’s just not like me, and at my age I don’t like when my routines start slipping like that.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities or foods you really liked before?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. It’s been one of the more upsetting parts, honestly, because those little things used to kind of hold my week together.

I used to really look forward to my watercolor class. I’d get my brushes rinsed and packed, pick out which paper I wanted, even think ahead about what colors I might use. And my quilting circle too — I’ve gone to that for years, and I used to enjoy just sitting with the ladies, working on a square, hearing everyone talk. Same with book club. Even if I hadn’t finished the whole book, I liked going and listening.

But lately I’ll get the bag ready, or at least I’ll mean to, and then it just sits by the door. I look at it and think, “I should go,” but there’s no pull there. I can’t seem to make myself care enough to actually leave the house for it. It’s not that I suddenly dislike those things. It’s more like the feeling that used to come with them just isn’t there right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days, and if so, how long does it usually last during the day?

Yes… most days, I think. Especially in the mornings. I wake up and there’s this heavy, low feeling already sitting there, before I’ve even gotten dressed or had coffee or opened the curtains. It’s like the color has gone out of the day before the day has even started, if that makes sense.

Sometimes it eases a little as the day goes on, if I get moving or there’s something I absolutely have to do, but the mornings are the worst. I just lie there for a bit thinking, “Oh, here we are again,” and it makes everything feel harder than it should.
How long have you been feeling this way most days — can you pinpoint when these feelings really started to take hold?

I’ve been trying to think back on that, because it didn’t feel like one day I woke up and everything had changed. It was more like it crept in and then, at some point, I realized it had become the usual way I felt.

I’d say it’s been about a year and two months now that this low, colorless stretch has really been with me most days. Maybe a little over a year, but fourteen months is the closest I can place it. It’s been long enough that I almost forget what my mornings used to feel like before it settled in.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or your weight over the past year?

Yes… the eating part especially. That’s actually one of the things that finally made me think, “All right, I probably need to talk to someone,” because it’s gotten very unlike me.

Some days I’ll just completely forget lunch. Not skip it on purpose, not because I’m trying to watch my weight or anything like that — I just look up and realize it’s late afternoon and I haven’t eaten a proper meal. And then other days it goes the other direction, where I’m standing at the kitchen counter eating crackers, or something sweet, just one thing after another, even though I’m not really enjoying it. It’s not even that it tastes good. It’s more like I’m just… doing it, if that makes sense.

Food doesn’t taste right the way it used to. I’ll make something I normally like, and I’ll take a few bites and think, “Well, that’s nothing.” Then later I’m picking at cookies or crackers out of the box like I’m looking for something in them that isn’t there.

So yes, my appetite has definitely been off. I’m not sure I’ve kept exact track of my weight the way I should, but my eating has been all turned around this past year.
Have you lost interest or felt no pleasure in almost all activities, even those you used to enjoy?

Yes… yes, I have. That’s actually been one of the sadder parts of it, because I used to be someone who had little things on the calendar that I looked forward to. Nothing grand, you know, but they mattered to me.

I used to go to watercolor class, and I’d get my brushes and paper together the night before, like it was something special. And my quilting circle — I knew the ladies there, we’d talk while we worked, and it was comforting. Book club too. Even if I hadn’t finished the whole book, I’d still want to go just to hear everyone talk.

Now I’ll sometimes pack the bag, or at least think I should pack it, and then it just sits by the door. I’ll look at it and think, “I should go,” but I can’t make myself care enough to actually pick it up and leave. It’s not that I hate those things now. It’s more like the feeling that used to pull me toward them just isn’t there most of the time. They seem far away somehow, even when they’re right there on the calendar.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth as much as you used to?

I don’t know that I’d put it exactly that way. I mean… I do get disappointed in myself sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s more than usual, or that it has that heavy kind of guilty feeling you’re asking about.

I’ll think, “Well, I should have gotten more done today,” or “I should have gone to that thing instead of staying home,” but it’s more like frustration or regret than feeling like I’m a terrible person. And as far as feeling worthless… no, I don’t think I’d say that. I don’t feel especially proud of myself lately, if that makes sense, but I don’t sit there thinking I have no value.

So… I guess the honest answer is, not really. Not in a way that stands out to me.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Yes… more on the slowed-down side, I think, though there are moments of the other thing too.

It’s like my body doesn’t quite get the message right away. I’ll decide I’m going to go from the living room to the kitchen, and it feels like it takes me longer than it should just to stand up, get my balance, and actually start walking. Crossing the room feels… not impossible, but slower, like I’m moving through thicker air or something. Even little things, like buttoning my sweater or getting my sleeves straight, can feel like they take twice as long as they used to.

And then, oddly, there are times I’m not exactly energetic, but I’ll pace around the house. I’ll have the same papers in my hand — mail or some list I meant to look at — and I’ll walk from one room to another and back again, not really doing anything with them. It’s not a productive kind of moving. It’s more like I can’t settle, but I also don’t feel full of energy. It’s a strange combination.
Have you had episodes of depression in the past, before this current period started?

I’m not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I don’t know if I would call anything before this an “episode,” exactly. I’ve had sad stretches in my life, like anybody does, and times where I was more down or discouraged, but I can’t quite say whether it was the same as what you mean clinically.

I suppose if you asked me, “Have you ever felt low before?” then yes, of course. But if you mean a real period like this current one, where it clearly started and went on in a way you could point to… I’m not sure. I don’t remember it that neatly. Nothing is coming to mind that I’d feel confident saying was a past depression episode.

Looking back, would you say there was ever a time before this current period when you felt down nearly every day, lost interest in things, and noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy for at least two weeks in a row?

I’m trying to think of a clean example, and I just… I don’t know that I can say yes to that. Not the way you’re describing it, with all of those things together and for two weeks straight.

I can remember times where I was down, certainly. I’ve had periods where I didn’t feel like myself, or I was quieter, or I didn’t enjoy things as much for a little while. But when you add in “nearly every day” and then sleep, appetite, energy changes all lined up for at least two weeks… I’m not sure. My memory doesn’t organize it that neatly.

There may have been times I complained I was tired or wasn’t sleeping right, but whether that was part of a depression kind of period, I really couldn’t say. I wouldn’t want to tell you yes just because it sounds possible. I just don’t have a definite one I can point to before now.
